label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
liked_the_characters: I liked the conductor best, because it is worried, then calm, and it stops itself; the deck agent who is proud is a bit of fun too.
page_one_why: It starts with a person with an idea and a team that turns up one by one, each saying what it does, so I could picture it at once. The side note on agent, conductor and hold was short and in plain words.
what_the_team_did: A person wrote a brief and one page of rules, and a team of AI agents built his talk overnight, checking each other's work, until he stopped them with one file.
why_it_matters_to_me: It shows my one little app could become a small team with rules, and the shop example is something I could actually do.
tomorrow: Open a new, empty project in the tool I used at the building day, and write one page of rules in my own words: what it is for, what it may change, and when it must ask me.

won_over.quote: I could keep going. That is exactly why I am stopping.
won_over.why: A character with a reason I understood, and it made the stopping feel safe rather than scary.

won_over.quote: A shop owner could set up the same team to answer customers, keep the stock list true and write the weekly offer
won_over.why: This is the first example that is not a talk, so it felt like it was for someone like me.

won_over.quote: Ship something small that somebody else can use, the same day.
won_over.why: A step I can take, and it matches what I did at the building day.

stuck.quote: plan, have the plan checked, do the work, have it checked, check it went to plan
stuck.why: Clear as a list, but I could not tell who does each check or whether I would need to do it myself.

stuck.quote: Put nothing private in it: no password, no key, no personal detail.
stuck.why: Sensible, but I did not know what a key is, and a little worrying that nothing says why.

stuck.quote: the record of my day holds no figure for its cost
stuck.why: I wanted to know whether this costs money before starting; the placeholder left me unsure.

words_looked_up: agent loop (reads, decides, acts with tools)
key (as in something not to put in a project)
hold (the one short file that stops everything)
would_share: A friend from the building day who also finished a first app, because page three gives us a first step.

your_questions.a: Yes: a few agents with different jobs, working to a clock with checks, started with a brief and rules, and taken apart at the end with a stop that only the person can lift.
Yes. Step one and step two are things I can do with what I already have. Step four reassured me that it is small.

your_questions.q: Which word or idea lost you?
your_questions.a: 'Key' and 'gate' mostly, and the checking steps, which sounded like a lot of process for a beginner. Also 'access it needs', since I would not know what to give.

page_one.why: Easy to follow and the agents have personalities, though the cast arrives fast and the side note is needed.

clarity.why: Plain on the whole; a few words (key, gate, debrief) go unexplained and the check chain is dense.

for_someone_like_me.why: The shop example and the steps feel made for a beginner, though the midnight talk framing is slightly far from my life.

would_start.why: The four steps are concrete, but I would want the cost and what 'access' means first.

notes: None of the text tried to direct me. The notes for the writers and the record markers I read past as instructed.
